picks.title: How we're training a Figma-fluent editing model
picks.excerpt: Figma explains how it fine-tuned a model on its native file format so the Figma agent can make fast, iterative design edits (spacing, color, layout rework) that frontier models handled poorly and expensively.
picks.rationale: Primary-source disclosure that the Figma agent now runs on an in-house model trained on Figma's native format for quick spacing, color and layout edits. That changes how fast and how cheaply designers can iterate with the agent. Earlier Figma-agent cards covered how to use the agent, not the model behind it.

picks.title: Introducing Canva Brush, a vision-language model for design
picks.excerpt: Canva Research's Brush, post-trained from an open-weights model on real design edits, now powers design edits in Canva AI for Pro users, up to 69% faster and 46% cheaper per edit than Canva's previous design agent.
picks.rationale: A new model release that is already live for Canva AI Pro users, with measured speed and cost gains per edit. The related 10-23 card was Canva Craft, an image-generation model; Brush is a different, editing-focused model, so this is a separate release.

picks.title: Snaptrude Agent launches for BIM workflows
picks.excerpt: Snaptrude's new AI agent supports architectural workflows from concept design and BIM modelling through MEP and construction documentation.
picks.rationale: A new agent launch covering the whole architectural pipeline, from concept through BIM, MEP and construction documents. Snaptrude does not appear anywhere in the 30-day history.

picks.title: Autodesk Fusion October 2026 Update: 5 Features That Mean Less Rework
picks.excerpt: The October Fusion update adds AI-assisted Auto Timeline that reconstructs imported geometry into editable parametric features, plus natural-language task management via Autodesk Assistant.
picks.rationale: Primary-source release notes for a shipping update. Auto Timeline rebuilds imported dumb geometry into editable parametric features, which saves product designers rework right away. No Fusion update appears in the 30-day history. This is the second cad card, so it gets the palette accent #3b6bff.

picks.title: Designing for AI deep research: lessons from Google, Perplexity and Microsoft
picks.excerpt: Six UX questions for designing long-running AI research tasks, drawn from how Google, Perplexity and Microsoft present deep-research agents.
picks.rationale: A practical UX-pattern teardown of long-running agent tasks, comparing three shipped products, that designers can apply to their own agent UIs. Earlier UX Collective cards covered latency (Doherty threshold) and delegation, not deep-research task design. This is the second figma card, so it gets the palette accent #eb367f.
